# 17-313 Foundations of Software Engineering — Syllabus (Fall 2026)

Students work in teams on a large existing open-source codebase (NodeBB, TypeScript/Node.js) across four projects.

## Learning objectives
- Use version control (git branches, merging, rebasing, pull requests) to collaborate on a shared codebase.
- Write and maintain automated tests (unit and integration), and reason about test adequacy (coverage, mutation testing).
- Set up and interpret continuous integration pipelines.
- Apply static analysis and type checking to find defects early.
- Elicit requirements and write user stories with acceptance criteria.
- Conduct and respond to code review.

## Schedule
- Weeks 1–3: Git and collaborative workflows (branches, merge vs rebase, conflict resolution, pull requests). Project 1 depends on this.
- Weeks 3–5: Testing — unit vs integration tests, test doubles and mocking, coverage and its limits, flaky tests. Projects 2–4 are graded partly on test quality.
- Week 6: Continuous integration (GitHub Actions), build failures, required checks.
- Week 7: Static analysis, linters, and TypeScript's type system (compile-time vs runtime).
- Week 8: Asynchronous JavaScript (promises, async/await, the event loop) as used throughout NodeBB.
- Weeks 9–10: Requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria.
- Week 11: Software architecture and design documentation.
- Week 12: Dependency management and semantic versioning (guest lecture).
- Weeks 13–14: Open source process, licensing, and team retrospectives.
